title: GPU Subsidy Headcount Hedge Playbook — Q4 2026
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sheet for creating a short-duration financial "subsidy" mechanism to smooth hiring and contractor decisions when GPU spot/lease prices spike. We model a reserve-backed subsidy pool that can be tapped automatically based on short triggers, and couple that to explicit headcount hedges so we avoid knee-jerk layoffs or expensive backfills during transient price shocks.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Create a $2.5M GPU Reserve (one-time allocation from Q4 flex) to fund time-limited subsidies and contractor top-ups for roles that materially reduce unit cost (serving runtime, SRE, infra ops).
- Trigger rules: 4-week rolling average GPU price > 120% of baseline or 10% sustained increase in per-token cost -> unlock tranche 1 (up to $800k).
- Headcount hedge: freeze non-critical hires after trigger; convert a pre-approved 20 FTE-equivalent contractor pool into a managed on-call/contract taper to cover throughput while preserving runway.
- Pricing sensitivity: baseline modeled, shock, and tail-down scenarios with headcount and cost impacts included.

Assumptions (base-case):
- Baseline average GPU lease-equivalent cost: $2.10 / GPU-hour (global mix).
- Baseline monthly GPU spend (prod serving + experiments): $420k / month.
- Baseline headcount (non-contract): 148 FTE; target hiring ramp next 12 months +22 FTE (primarily infra & serving runtime).
- Contractor hourly uplift (market): 1.6x equivalent full-time unit cost when used for surge.

Scenario matrix (high-level):
1) Base case (no subsidy): GPU price = $2.10/hr, monthly GPU spend $420k; planned hires proceed (Q4 hires = 6).
2) Shock case (no subsidy): GPU price = $3.50/hr (+67%), monthly GPU spend $700k; immediate margin erosion ~7.8 pts; recommended hiring freeze and 25% feature-scope deferral.
3) Subsidy-backed shock (proposed): Tap tranche 1 ($800k) to cover 3 months of incremental GPU cost and contractor top-ups; hiring freeze relaxed for 2 hires critical to cost reduction (quantization & batching infra).
4) Tail-down case: GPU price drops to $1.30/hr (spot dislocation); convert contractors to hires where retention value is high and precommit capacity/discounts negotiated.

Quick numeric sensitivity (illustrative):
- Per 10% increase in GPU price -> incremental monthly GPU spend +$42k (base mix).
- Incremental monthly GPU spend converted to gross margin drag: approx 0.9–1.1% points per +10% price (depends on revenue mix).
- If GPU price +67% (shock), expected run-rate headcount savings needed to hold margin flat ~18–22 FTE (if only staffing changes used), which is operationally undesirable.

Headcount hedge details (playbook items):
- Priority roles to protect: Serving Runtime Engineers (4 hires), SRE (2 hires), Quantization/Model Ops (3 hires). Rationale: direct and persistent unit cost reduction potential.
- Candidates for flexible contractor coverage: Data labeling & non-core infra (convertible contractors, up to 20 FTE-equivalent).
- Hiring cadence adjustments: instead of immediate hires, stagger offers with 8–12 week windows and conditional start dates tied to 12w rolling GPU price.
- Conversion policy: if 12-week average GPU price < 95% baseline and role performance rated >=3.5, convert contractor to FTE with prorated signing bonus from reserve.

Subsidy mechanics and governance:
- Reserve size: $2.5M (one-time capital from Q4 flex).
- Tranches: Tranche 1 = $800k (fast unlock), Tranche 2 = $1.2M (requires CFO + CEO sign-off), Residual = $500k (strategic precommit/coupon pool for partner discounts).
- Unlock criteria: automated signal from cost telemetry pipeline (console metric: cluster-gpu-hour-spot-index) and finance confirmation.
- Uses allowed: direct GPU cost reimbursements for committed projects, contractor top-ups tied to serving throughput, limited hiring sign-on top-ups for retained critical hires.
- Prohibited uses: general payroll, long-term headcount expansion unrelated to cost mitigation.

Budget sheet excerpt (monthly run-rate snapshot, $k):
- Base-case GPU spend: 420
- Shock delta (+67%): 280
- Subsidy tranche 1 available monthly coverage for delta (if fully used over 3 months): 266 = 800/3
- Contractor pool top-up (estimate) monthly: 60
- Net reserve burn over 3 months: ~740 (includes administrative buffers)

Operational levers (ordered by speed to value):
1) Routing & batching config tweaks (runtime changes) — immediate, low headcount cost, medium risk to tail latency.
2) Quantization pilot ramp (model ops) — 4–8 weeks to materially reduce per-token cost for inference-heavy customers.
3) Precommit/discount negotiations with cloud vendors for core-serving fleets — 6–12 weeks.
4) Temporary contractor pool activation — 1–2 weeks.

Pricing sensitivity experiments to run (A/B):
- Small customer cohort (5% of revenue) move to quantized model variant for 2 weeks; measure per-token cost and quality delta.
- Route-level throttle + caching experiment to measure percent traffic reducible without customer-visible regressions.
- Offer optional burst credits to enterprise customers to shift peak tails (test price elasticity for surge-priced requests).

Open questions / risks (notes to reviewers):
- How to instrument per-feature unit economics quickly enough to map GPU price spikes to product-level margins? Need a 2-week telemetry sprint.
- Behavioral risk: customers could game surge credits; policy needs per-account caps and expiration rules.
- Legal/compliance review for contractor conversion terms (immigration/visa implications).
- Tax treatment of one-time signing top-ups vs. operational subsidies.

Recommended next steps (immediate):
- Finance & Product ops to stand up a 2-week telemetry sprint: deliver per-route unit-econ dashboard (owner: Priya).
- Legal to review contractor conversion & subsidy mechanics (owner: Ethan).
- SRE + Serving runtime to deliver 2 quick batching+cache knobs we can flip in 72 hours (owner: Jordan).
- CFO + CEO to approve reserve headroom and tranche thresholds for emergency fast-unlock.

Notes to self / raw numbers used in modeling (scratch):
- Model inputs saved in linked artifact (cost-models repo, branch gpu-reserve-sim). See PR #56 for formulas.
- Sensitivity table used: base | +10% | +25% | +50% | +67% with monthly GPU spend scaled proportionally to GPU-hours mix.

Status & communication plan:
- This doc is a working sheet (in_review). Goal: align Finance/Product/SRE on tranche mechanics and telemetry sprint by 2026-11-16.
- If accepted, convert to canonical playbook and publish to Confluence with step-by-step runbook and automation links.

-- end of working sheet --
